source_title: Nokia Sells Devices Business to Microsoft
publisher_issuer: Light Reading; corroborated by Nokia SEC Form 6-K filings (CIK 0000924613)
company_context: Nokia, once the world's dominant mobile-handset maker, failed to respond effectively to the iPhone and Android and lost its smartphone leadership. Rather than collapse, it sold its Devices & Services business to Microsoft and pivoted to its remaining businesses, principally Nokia Networks (telecom infrastructure), plus HERE maps and Technologies/patents.
macro_context: Smartphone platform shift to iOS/Android; feature-phone collapse; consolidation in telecom network infrastructure (with Ericsson, Huawei).
evidence_summary: Nokia's Devices & Services business generated about EUR 14.9 billion ($19.6 billion) revenue in 2012 but carried an operating loss exceeding EUR 1 billion. In September 2013 Nokia agreed to sell that business to Microsoft for about EUR 5.44 billion ($7.2 billion), with roughly 32,000 employees transferring; the deal closed in 2014. Nokia survived by pivoting to three remaining businesses, led by Nokia Networks, exiting the loss-making handset operation. The outcome was mixed: the iconic handset business was lost, but the company endured as a profitable network-equipment firm.
owner_decision_context: Nokia leadership decided to exit the structurally loss-making handset business by selling it to Microsoft and redeploying around the profitable Networks unit rather than continuing to fund handset losses.
action_taken: Sold the Devices & Services (handset) business to Microsoft for ~EUR 5.44 billion and pivoted the company to Networks/HERE/Technologies, surviving via the network-equipment business.
outcome_evidence: Exit of a >EUR 1 billion operating-loss business and refocus on Networks allowed Nokia to survive as a profitable infrastructure company, a partial/mixed outcome: the core consumer franchise was lost but the firm endured.
source_limitations: WebFetch unavailable (403 pattern); figures confirmed across Light Reading, Slidebean, and Nokia SEC Form 6-K snippets (CIK 0000924613). The handset operating-loss and unit figures are reported approximations from the period; precise audited annual figures not fetched in full text.
directly_stated: Devices & Services had ~EUR 14.9 billion ($19.6B) revenue in 2012 with >EUR 1 billion operating loss
Nokia sold the business to Microsoft for ~EUR 5.44 billion ($7.2B); ~32,000 employees transferred
Nokia refocused on Networks, HERE, and Technologies
inferred: Exiting handsets was a strategic pivot that preserved the firm (survival) but ended its consumer leadership (mixed)
The Networks business provided the durable, profitable core
why_useful_for_opsiq: Outcome-5 partial/mixed case: a major business decline managed via divestiture and pivot to survive. Tests whether the engine credits a strategic pivot that preserves the enterprise while acknowledging loss of the original franchise, without labeling it a clean failure or turnaround.
